text:
nicole: quick one - noticed our starter package blows up types when used in edge (nodenext/ESM) builds. CJS + node16 projects are fine. anyone seen this?

raj: yep. nodenext and bundlers disagree on how to resolve .d.ts for conditional exports. what's your package.json exports + tsconfig?

nicole: package.json: ```json
{"name":"@redwood/starter","exports":{"import":"./dist/esm/index.mjs","require":"./dist/cjs/index.cjs"},"types":"dist/types/index.d.ts"}
``` tsconfig: ```json
{"compilerOptions":{"module":"nodenext","moduleResolution":"nodenext","declaration":true,"emitDeclarationOnly":true,"outDir":"dist","composite":true}}
```

kai: emitDeclarationOnly + composite is fine, but nodenext emits file names like index.d.ts vs index.mjs.d.ts depending on bundler. some consumers (vite/esbuild) prefer the .mjs path and lookup a corresponding d.ts that we don't produce. result: IDE falls back and shows `any`.

sam: also watch `types` vs `exports`. If you have conditional exports you should either point `types` to a generic entry under `dist` that both import/require resolve to, or add `typesVersions` to map ESM consumers. otherwise Node's resolver won't pick up the correct declarations.

raj: second gotcha: if your implementation uses `any` in the function body, the emitted d.ts may widen generic overloads. example I hit: ```ts
export function parse(x: string): string;
export function parse<T>(x: T): T;
export function parse(x: any) { return x }
```
tsserver sometimes shows parse as (x: any) => any after bundling because a post-processing step rewrites overloads. using `unknown` in impl or better, strongly-typed implementation, helps keep signatures.

kai: fwiw we solved similar by: build script emits declarations to dist/types, then we copy a flat index.d.ts into both dist/esm and dist/cjs during postbuild. also added a tiny tsd test that imports the package from `dist/esm` and asserts types. catches regressions in CI.

nicole: that sounds reasonable. curious about adding typesVersions — any config example?

sam: example: ```json
{"typesVersions": {"*": {"*": ["dist/types/*"]}}}
```
This makes TypeScript prefer those types for all import styles. Pair with `types` pointing at `dist/types/index.d.ts` so non-TS consumers still work.

raj: if we go further, consider emitting dual declaration sets: one with nodenext-style filenames (index.mjs.d.ts) and one plain index.d.ts. annoying but robust. also document that starter uses `moduleResolution: bundler` in dev for faster editor behavior.

kai: one more nuance: some bundlers strip type-only exports or inline helpers; if you re-export generics across packages (export type { X } from 'pkg') ensure `preserveValueImports` and `isolatedModules` interplay doesn't drop the shape.

nicole: ok i'll draft a PR: postbuild copy + tsd test + README note about nodenext vs bundler. will also try typesVersions approach first to see if we can avoid duplicate d.ts.

build-bot: opened issue #472: "starter: nodenext/ESM declaration resolution mismatch in edge runtime" and created branch: starter/472-esm-types.

sam: thanks. if you want i can add a small GitHub Actions job that runs `tsc -p tsd` against the built dist/esm entry to catch the `any` collapse in CI. saved me a few times.

nicole: please do. assigning to eng-devex for review. will post PR link once ready.
